ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against: (i) Egyptian AML/CFT list published by the Central Bank of Egypt; (ii) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) OFAC SDN list; (iv) Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority blacklists; and (v) domestic terrorist-financing lists issued under Egyptian law. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, immediate family member known associate, or any person connected to a high-risk jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) -- Online Company Registration Portal at https://www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Arabic is the mandatory language for the legal name of the Egyptian LLC. The Arabic name must be written in the Arabic script without internal punctuation, may include the trade name in Latin characters only as a supplementary commercial name, and must not cause confusion with an existing registered trademark or business name. Non-Arabic corporate names must be transliterated into Arabic in accordance with GAFI and Commercial Registry transliteration rules. The English name must be a direct word-for-word transliteration of the Arabic name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Grievance Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the original rejection notice, a revised name application (in Arabic), a certified copy of the applicant's commercial passport or power of attorney, and a legal memorandum demonstrating non-confusion, non-infringement, and compliance with Decree No. 159 of 1981 executive regulations and the Commercial Registry Law. The Grievance Committee must issue a decision within 15 working days of the complete appeal. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate a legal challenge before the Egyptian Administrative Court within 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is generally not accepted for the principal registered office in Egypt. The registered office must be a physical place accessible by the Commercial Registry and applicable tax authorities, and must have a physical sign bearing the company name. For a hyper-casual gaming monoline, a dedicated serviced office or a mailbox-only arrangement is conditionally permitted only for service-of-process purposes if a full operational address is separately maintained and disclosed to the Egyptian Tax Authority. A purely virtual address lacking any local substance will not satisfy the registered-obligation test and will be treated as non-compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: estimated risk of unannounced on-site inspection by GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, or the Social Insurance Authority is approximately 30% during the first 12 months of operation. Inspection probability increases if the company files for VAT registration, employs resident staff, or receives material bank inflows from abroad.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; relevant Articles including Articles 8-14, 21-30 and their Executive Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Commercial Registry Department; for LLC formations, GAFI One-Stop-Shop is the exclusive incorporation authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation and Articles of Association (طلب تأسيس وعقد الشركة) submitted through GAFI Form GAFI-02.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a Limited Liability Company under Egyptian law; the capital is determined in the Articles of Association. For cash subscriptions, not less than 50% of the subscribed capital must be deposited into a bank account opened in the company's name before registration; the balance must be fully paid within five years from incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founders' subscriptions to the company's share capital, as specified in the Articles of Association, are hereby ratified and accepted; the allocation of shares to each subscribing shareholder is approved. (2) The registered office identified in the incorporation filings is adopted as the company's legal seat and principal place of business within Egypt; its address shall be used for all statutory correspondence and regulatory notices. (3) The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Company Secretary, with authorization to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the company before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Civil Defense Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade Name Reservation and Legal Structure Pre-Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Portal / One-Stop-Shop Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request together with the provisional Articles of Association and shareholder identity documents. GAFI will validate the corporate name, legal form, and activity code. Documents may be notarized directly after pre-validation.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Passport or national ID of each founding shareholder
Power of attorney if submitted by a local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, amend the flagged corporate name, clarify the activity classification, and resubmit the same application within 15 working days without the need for a new request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Bank Deposit Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt; the deposit certificate is then submitted to GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital contribution account in the intended company name at a licensed Egyptian bank and deposit not less than 50% of the subscribed cash capital. Obtain the bank's capital deposit certificate confirming the amount and the account holder's intent to form the LLC.
required_dossiers: Resolution of founders on capital allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC or source of funds documentation, furnish the shareholders' bank statements and source-of-funds declaration; the capital certificate can be reissued after such documentation is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and GAFI Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Katib Al-Adl) and then GAFI One-Stop-Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After capital confirmation, present the Articles of Association to the Notary Public for authentication. Then submit the notarized Articles, capital certificate, and proof of registered office to GAFI for issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and entry in the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Copy of lease contract or proof of right to use the registered office
GAFI-02 incorporation application with statutory declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a query on the Articles or supporting documents, file a formal explanatory response and amended signature pages within 20 working days; failure to cure may be remedied by refiling the dossier under the same pre-validation file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and VAT Registration at the Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) post-registration window, coordinated through GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registry extract to the ETA to obtain the Tax Card (regulating income tax, payroll tax, and stamp duty) and complete VAT registration if annual supplies are expected to exceed the mandatory threshold. Include the company bank account details and registered office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Card is delayed or queried, correct any mismatches in the registered address or legal representative information and resubmit the ETA form; an expedited appeal may be lodged with the ETA public services department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance and Municipal Office Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and the local district office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the new LLC as an employer with NOSI and file the founders and initial employees for mandatory social insurance coverage. Obtain the municipal occupancy permit or business registration certificate from the local district office where the registered office is located.
required_dossiers: Lease contract registered with the Official Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI rejects any employee registration, correct the national ID or contract date, pay any late or recalculated contribution, and resubmit the Dafhtar forms through the NOSI online portal within 30 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the scope of software publishing for ad-monetized mobile games does not constitute an industrial establishment; GAFI remains the competent authority for activity amendments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no manufacturing or operational trade license is required for an office-based game publishing company under Egyptian law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category D (non-polluting service/commercial activity); software publishing is not listed in the applicable EIA operations schedule and therefore no environmental registration or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the operation produces no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste; standard office waste must be disposed of through licensed municipal collection services and clearance letters are obtained for server/equipment disposal if needed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) is required for the registered office, issued after inspection under Law No. 205 of 2020. The local district office and the Ministry of Manpower may also require an occupational workplace clearance, including structural load confirmation, means of egress, and fire extinguisher/emergency lighting compliance, before employees commence onsite work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official portal: www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing an Egyptian LLC must apply to ETA for a tax card, commercial registration certificate, and VAT ID. Application forms require notarized constitutional documents, lease contracts, foreign investment approval (if required), and proof of address. ETA issues a unified tax identification number (TIN) for income tax, VAT, and payroll purposes
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election under Egyptian law; entity is taxed as a corporation per Law 91 of 2005. Hybrid mismatch rules follow OECD BEPS recommendations; election opportunities limited to thin capitalization and transfer pricing advance pricing agreements

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies (goods and services) unless excluded by special regimes for non-resident e-services providers
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for all VAT-registered taxpayers transacting with B2B/B2G partners; invoices must be transmitted in real time to the ETA e-invoice portal with API integration (JSON/XML), cryptographic digital stamping, and fiscal clearance before use. E-receipts are mandatory for consumer sales in phased rollout

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of software and digital game publishing services qualify for 0% VAT when services are supplied for use outside Egypt, the payment is received in foreign convertible currency, and the services are not connected with Egyptian territorial consumption. The exporter must be able to evidence that the recipient is a non-resident and that the actual consumption occurs abroad
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for physical goods; not applicable for pure digital services)
Signed service agreement or contract with foreign customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) evidencing receipt in foreign exchange
Record of platform payout statements (e.g., AdMob/AppLovin) showing source and deduction of withholding or commissions
Apostilled or notarized proof of non-resident recipient status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims are scrutinized by ETA with retrospective recovery of VAT due at 14%, plus delay interest, fines up to 200% of tax evaded, and criminal penalties for tax evasion under Law No. 67 of 2016; responsible directors may face imprisonment and asset freezing orders

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole sovereign monetary, banking-licensing and foreign-exchange control authority in the Arab Republic of Egypt, with powers derived from Law No. 88 of 2003 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) as amended and recodified by Law No. 194 of 2020 (Foreign Exchange Regulation). The General Authority for Investment (GAFI) governs investment registration and foreign-capital entry, while the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) supervises non-bank financial institutions. Every cross-border treasury transaction of the Egyptian resident limited liability company must be executed through a CBE-authorized bank of exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the 6 March 2024 flexible exchange-rate reform anchored by the IMF EFF programme, the Egyptian Pound is a unified, market-determined currency with full legal convertibility for current-account transactions: ad-network proceeds (Google AdMob, AppLovin), software royalties and services receipts may be credited and repatriated in USD, EUR or EGP through the authorized banking system without prior CBE licence, at the interbank rate. Residual capital-account gates remain: (i) foreign shareholder loans should be documented on arm's-length terms and supported by executed facility agreements; (ii) dividend remittances require an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax-clearance certificate confirming settlement of the 10% statutory withholding, or a treaty-reduced rate, plus a bank-of-exchange FX purpose form; (iii) CBE circulars restrict physical foreign-currency cash deposit and withdrawal channels but do not constrain SWIFT-clearing corporate transfers; (iv) the 2022-23 import L/C-only restrictions were abolished, leaving no quantitative limits on current-account outward payments. The net assessment is unrestricted convertibility for a low-risk digital-services exporter, subject only to documentary and tax-clearance compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The CBE no longer imposes any statutory surrender percentage or mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts. Pursuant to the 2023 ministerial measures and the March 2024 unified-FX regime, the Egyptian exporter may retain one hundred percent of foreign-currency proceeds in its USD/EUR corporate accounts and convert at the interbank rate when EGP funds are required. Repatriation is nevertheless obligatory: all export and ad-network proceeds must be credited through an Egyptian licensed bank of exchange within the CBE benchmark collection window - approximately 120 days from the service-rendition date for digital and software exports, with longer windows for goods exports subject to CBE-endorsed extensions - and must be supported by the registered export form, platform settlement statements and bank-of-exchange documentation. Delinquent repatriation triggers adverse CBE reporting, enhanced AML/CFT scrutiny and potential suspension of subsequent inward-clearing approvals.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational EGP and USD current accounts
Operational EGP/USD/EUR current accounts; trade settlement facilities
Operational USD current account; treasury and FX line

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 April for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment surcharge of 2% per month of the unpaid tax due, capped at 100% of the tax; unresolved obligations can trigger administrative enforcement and a potential strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and annual activity report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Filing Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end, with a final GAFI submission within 30 days of approval by the Shareholders' General Assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI administrative delay penalties; prolonged non-filing may lead to suspension of commercial registration and loss of legal capacity to transact.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration annual fee and quinquennial data renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office - Ministry of Trade and Industry (via GAFI One-Stop Shop)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual fee payable on the commercial registration anniversary; substantive data renewal every 5 years before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Registry Law 34/1976 delay fines; suspension of the commercial registry record, preventing the LLC from executing binding contracts or renewing operational licenses.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all limited liability companies in Egypt without minimum capital or turnover exemption; an independent auditor licensed with the Egyptian Federation of Accountants and Auditors must be appointed before the annual General Assembly meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by Decree No. 110 of 2015, converged with IFRS; IFRS may be adopted by listed or multinational entities subject to Financial Regulatory Authority approval.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt does not require a standalone annual UBO report; however, per AML Law 80/2002 the LLC must maintain a current ultimate beneficial owner register and notify the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit of any material changes or share transfers within 30 days. UBO details are reconfirmed annually at the General Assembly before dividend approval.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assembly Meetings
Register of Contracts with Directors and Related Parties

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory rate of 22.5% under Law No. 91 of 2005 (Income Tax Law), as amended. Preferential reductions: (1) Free-Zone projects licensed under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 may obtain 100% CIT exemption on commercial and industrial profits; (2) projects located in priority governorates may deduct up to 50% of investment costs from taxable income; (3) technology and software development companies may qualify for the unified investment incentives (golden license), including special deductions for fixed-asset investments; (4) no effective rate reduction is granted specifically to hyper-casual gaming publishers outside these zones, so the headline 22.5% applies unless an incentive license is secured.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 19 (Legal Persons) filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-portal at tax.gov.eg; paper submission only at the competent tax office where electronic access is unavailable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months following the fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 April for a 31 December year-end); the ETA may grant an additional 2-month extension upon a written, justified request submitted before the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Tax Identification Number (TIN) and Tax Card
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records the LLC's TIN, tax card number, commercial registration number, legal form code, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent must verify that the Egyptian LLC holds a valid tax card and that the TIN matches the beneficiary data used on AdMob/AppLovin payout accounts; any mismatch triggers automatic bank-side withholding defects.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregates all worldwide commercial receipts of the Egyptian LLC, including gross advertising revenue settled by AdMob (Google) and AppLovin before platform commissions, in-game purchase revenues, and any related-party service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report ad-network payouts gross of platform deductions; attach monthly payout statements from AdMob/AppLovin and a reconciliation schedule showing deducible platform fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims ordinary and necessary expenses: developer salaries, cloud hosting, user-acquisition costs, software license royalties, depreciation of equipment and intangible assets, borrowing costs, and statutory social insurance contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalty and interest expenses paid to non-residents are deductible only if the WHT has been withheld and remitted; apply for the reduced treaty WHT rate before payment and attach the ETA clearance certificate to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Taxable Income After Loss Set-Off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes net taxable income after ordinary tax-loss carry-forward (maximum 5 fiscal years) and after applying any investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward continuity must be evidenced by ownership registers; a change of more than 50% in foreign ultimate ownership may disqualify the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Income Tax at Headline Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the 22.5% CIT rate to taxable income; separately shows any branch tax or supplementary tax liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 32.5% rate for petroleum and mining activities is not applicable; treaty-reduced or free-zone-exempt income must cite the ETA approval letter and supporting TRC attached to the file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Advance Tax Payments and Withholding Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsets advance CIT payments (Form 15 receipts), payroll WHT offsets, and WHT credits on Egyptian-source interest or royalties received by the LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot apply personal tax credits to the LLC's CIT; any refund claim for excess prepayment must be filed separately with the ETA's refund committee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EGP 20,000, plus a delay surcharge of 2% for each calendar month on the unpaid tax. Late payment: additional 2%-per-month surcharge, not capped by the duration of delay, in accordance with Articles 132-133 of Law 91/2005; failure to submit the TP Disclosure Form (Form 21) separately triggers a fine up to EGP 20,000 and may elevate the matter to criminal evasion proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% gross-basis withholding tax on dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders (Law 91/2005, Art. 58); the rate applies to cash and deemed distributions and is reduced under applicable double tax agreements, generally to 5-15% depending on ownership levels.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for DTA relief the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the relevant fiscal year from the residence jurisdiction; (2) submit a treaty-relief application form to the ETA Claims Department, accompanied by the TRC, audited financial statements, certificate of incorporation, and a beneficial-ownership declaration; (3) evidence actual shareholding satisfying the treaty minimum holding period (often 10-25%); and (4) obtain the ETA's written reduction approval before the dividend distribution is remitted. The payer may apply the reduced WHT rate only after the ETA certificate has been issued; retroactive refunds are available within the 5-year statute of limitation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 20%, interest 20%, and service/contract consideration paid to non-resident providers 20%. Treaty rates: royalties typically 10-15% (e.g., US-Egypt DTA: 15% on industrial royalties); interest typically 10-15% with complete exemption available under several DTAs for loans granted by governmental financial institutions; reduced treaty WHT requires the same ETA prior-approval and TRC process. For hyper-casual gaming operations, royalties paid for game engine licenses (e.g., Unity, Unreal) or in-house IP to foreign related parties are fully subject to WHT assessment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 1,000,000: TP Disclosure Form (Form 21) must be attached to the annual CIT return when aggregate related-party transactions reach this threshold. EGP 5,000,000: Local File documentation mandatory for controlled transactions above this threshold. Group consolidated turnover above EGP 1,000,000,000: Master File required. Groups with consolidated revenue above EGP 5,000,000,000: Country-by-Country Report filing applies, coordinated with the OECD Automatic Exchange of Information network.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime as in UAE; however, Article 143 of Law 91/2005 contains a General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) empowering the ETA to disregard transactions or legal forms lacking genuine commercial substance. For an EG LLC active in hyper-casual gaming, the ETA will test: physical office presence, payroll and social insurance registrations of local developers, board minutes approving AdMob/AppLovin agreements, control over game code and IP ownership, and real decision-making for user-acquisition spending. A foreign-owned LLC functioning solely as a revenue pass-through without economic activity will be re-characterized as a permeable agent, denying treaty benefits and exposing profits to full 22.5% CIT plus 20% WHT on deemed distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Understatement of Digital Advertising Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of AdMob/AppLovin payout statements from the CIT return, routing ad revenue to private foreign bank accounts, or classifying gross advertising receipts as non-taxable advances to evade the 22.5% CIT charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine equal to the full amount of the evaded tax and no less than EGP 10,000 and no more than EGP 50,000, plus imprisonment for a term of up to 5 years (Law 91/2005, Art. 133); additionally, the ETA imposes a 2%-monthly delay surcharge on the unpaid tax and may compound penalty interest through judicial attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general manager who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax under the Egyptian Tax Collection Law; the ETA may apply for precautionary asset freezes, obtain a travel ban against each responsible director, and criminal conviction disqualifies the individual from managing any Egyptian legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Egyptian LLC as a hollow invoice pass-through for foreign ad networks while actual game development, marketing decisions, and IP control remain with a zero-tax foreign parent, and distributing profits under a treaty rate without real local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disregards the LLC under Article 143 GAAR, reattributes the profits to the foreign principal, denies all treaty reductions, and assesses 22.5% CIT on the re-attributed income plus 20% WHT on deemed dividends and royalties, with the 2%-per-month delay surcharge; additional fines range from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 depending on the financial benefit obtained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors executing sham service and licensing agreements may be pierced; the court can impose personal civil restitution for the re-attributed tax, order the release of bank guarantees, impose imprisonment where false declarations about substance are proven, and freeze personal assets pending final tax litigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's-Length Mispricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 21, absence of Local File, or mispricing the intercompany royalty/user-acquisition fee base to shift profit to the foreign parent, e.g., paying an inflated 40% royalty for internally developed game engines, or allocating user-acquisition costs wrongly to the Egyptian entity without arm's-length benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA upward adjustment under the approved OECD methodologies (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split); additional charge of the full CIT deficiency at 22.5%, plus a 2%-monthly delay surcharge; separate administrative fine up to EGP 20,000 for missing documentation; if the mispricing is shown to be intentional, the evasion penalties and imprisonment provisions of Art. 133 apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The TP adjustment binds the LLC, but directors who knowingly certified the absence of controlled transactions in Form 21 may be personally liable for the differential where corporate assets are insufficient; ETA enforcement includes personal bank attachment, travel bans on the financial officer, and in flagrant cases criminal referral for false attestation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Unlicensed Payment Intermediation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using private foreign payout accounts for AdMob/AppLovin proceeds without linking them to the Egyptian LLC's TIN, or processing high-volume ad-revenue payouts outside the Egyptian banking system without proper AML registration and transaction reporting under Law No. 80/2002, as amended by Law No. 36/2017 and Central Bank regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Confiscation of the laundered funds; fine of up to EGP 1,000,000 or double the value of the funds, whichever is greater; imprisonment from 5 to 10 years for persons convicted of money laundering; additionally, ETA blocks the foreign payout chain without reopening an Egyptian bank account, and the tax authority retroactively assesses 22.5% CIT plus 20% repatriation WHT on the cleansed amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable solely on the basis of negligent oversight of payment flows even without personal benefit; a conviction cancels banking mandates, imposes a travel ban, disqualifies the director from future Egyptian financial institution roles, and creates a statutory lien over personal assets to settle the tax arrears.
